_catatan: Public Narrative Brief on Forest and Land Fires 2026 for the Head of BNPB, rebuilt from the 031126 deck with BNPB data as of 2 Nov 2026 and the latest official sources.
pesan_kunci: The 2026 fire season is the worst since 2019 and is under national command; prevention targets peatland, arsonists are pursued up to corporations, and foreign help enters through one BNPB channel.

slide.pesan: A severe season, handled by Indonesia itself, focused on peatland and perpetrators

slide.tesis: The Government of Indonesia leads the 2026 response to forest and land fires and concentrates it on peatland areas. Individuals and corporations that deliberately burn land are pursued; foreign assistance is coordinated under government command.

temuan.teks: Firespots in 2026 reach {{angka:fs.kali_2019|fmt=1}} times 2019 and {{angka:fs.persen_2015|fmt=0|persen}} of 2015.
One third of the points lie in peatland areas; dry peat makes fires hard to extinguish, so the response is concentrated on peatland.
Bareskrim Polri has named {{angka:karhutla.hukum.korporasi_tersangka}} corporations and {{angka:karhutla.hukum.perorangan}} individuals as suspects in 2026 forest and land fire cases.

The response is a joint effort: {{angka:karhutla.personel_pemerintah}} personnel from government units (TNI, Polri, BPBD, local government, Manggala Agni, Forest Police) and {{angka:karhutla.personel_nonpem}} from community groups (company crews, volunteers, Fire Care Community).

daftar: Peat embers spread beneath the surface, so fires are hard to put out from above.
Peatland is considered degraded when its water table drops more than {{angka:karhutla.muka_air_cm|fmt=0}} cm below the surface; at that point peat is dry and burns easily.
The number of forest and land fire incidents rises sharply when average rainfall during the dry season is below {{angka:karhutla.hujan_ambang|fmt=0|satuan}}.
The 2015 losses were about US${{angka:karhutla.biaya_per_ha_2015}} per ha, with losses of US${{angka:karhutla.biaya_2015|fmt=1}} billion (World Bank); this figure is the basis of the 2026 projection.

kolom.isi: Peat left to dry out burns easily; the fire spreads beneath the surface and the smoke travels far.
The 2026 bar is a satellite-based projection to 3 November; the official area follows once the season ends.
Indonesia has {{angka:karhutla.khg_n}} peatland areas covering {{angka:karhutla.khg_luas|fmt=1|satuan}}.

daftar: Licence holders must prevent and extinguish fires in their areas.
Hotspots in concession areas are the basis for investigation by Forestry law enforcement and Bareskrim Polri.
Industrial timber plantations account for the most concession hotspots; oil palm plantations come second.
Oil palm is a strategic commodity; action is taken against individuals who burn, especially on peatland.

{{angka:karhutla.hukum.korporasi_asing}} suspect corporations have foreign capital and face the same law as domestic ones.

slide.judul: Overseas partnership: assistance is welcomed with appreciation, and operational sovereignty comes first

isi.teks: Humanitarian assistance from abroad is welcomed with appreciation and handled with care.
Assistance operations can be used to gauge response capacity and map territory.
National interest and operational sovereignty are the first priority.
Partnerships with friendly countries continue on an equal footing.
We are open to partnerships that are equal and mutually respectful.
Operational sovereignty rests with BNPB in accordance with Indonesian law.
This is a mandate of the law and is not negotiable.
All assistance works under the command of the Government of Indonesia.

slide.judul: Ten recommendations for overseas partnership guidelines {{sorot:(1/2)}}
slide.sumber: Law 24/2007; GR 23/2008; GR 4/2018; BNPB foreign partnership guide, Nov 2026

rekomendasi.langkah: Affirm BNPB as the single coordinator
rekomendasi.rincian: BNPB leads coordination under the Disaster Management Law; other countries act as supporters.
Water bombing aircraft, logistics, funds and personnel are recorded through BNPB; direct channels to regional governments or NGOs are avoided.

rekomendasi.langkah: Accept assistance in a balanced way
rekomendasi.rincian: Assistance from the United States and China as well as Japan, Malaysia, Australia and Singapore is accepted together so that none becomes dominant.

rekomendasi.langkah: Request lists of personnel and equipment
rekomendasi.rincian: Names, identities, equipment, sensors, drones, radio frequencies and flight routes are submitted before operations begin.
Every team from another country is accompanied by BNPB or TNI personnel in the field, including an official interpreter.

slide.judul: Ten recommendations for overseas partnership guidelines {{sorot:(2/2)}}
slide.sumber: Law 24/2007; GR 23/2008; GR 4/2018; BNPB foreign partnership guide, Nov 2026

rekomendasi.langkah: Set limits on areas of access
rekomendasi.rincian: Papua and border regions, including sensitive concession areas, may be entered only with written permission from the competent authority or the Head of BNPB.
Assistance uses local logistics, food, fuel and labour to support the domestic economy.
Media releases through BNPB and the Intermestic forum highlight national capacity; weaknesses in logistics and data systems are not discussed with other countries.

rekomendasi.langkah: Promote technology transfer and time limits
rekomendasi.rincian: Assistance comes with training for Indonesian personnel and agreed start and end dates.

rekomendasi.langkah: Involve other ministries and report to leadership
rekomendasi.rincian: Foreign data is checked before it leaves Indonesia; results are reported to the President through the Coordinating Minister, with no new bilateral commitments before central approval.

slide.pesan: Guide to three types of documents
slide.judul: Humanitarian operations use civil MoUs under BNPB; SOFA and VFA are matters for the central government

utama.judul: Guide to three types of documents

isi.teks: **Memorandum of Understanding**: a civil cooperation memorandum, without military immunity.
Signed by BNPB with partner institutions.
The mechanism BNPB uses.
**Status of Forces Agreement**: an agreement between states on the legal status of foreign military personnel while in Indonesia.
Concerns jurisdiction and sovereignty.
Not signed at BNPB level.
**Visiting Forces Agreement**: an agreement on visits by foreign forces for temporary military exercises, similar to a SOFA.
Decided by the central government through the Foreign and Defence Ministries.
Not within BNPB's authority.

panel.judul: Key sentences if offered a SOFA
daftar: We greatly appreciate the offer of assistance.
For humanitarian operations, we use civil mechanisms under BNPB in accordance with the Disaster Management Law.
Agreements on the status of forces are the authority of the central government through the Foreign and Defence Ministries, and are not decided in a disaster management partnership forum.
The offer of assistance continues to be processed through BNPB's civil mechanisms.

slide.judul: Talking Point: Welcoming Australian Assistance for Forest and Land Fire Response in East Kalimantan {{sorot:(1/3)}}
slide.sumber: Head of BNPB talking points, Nov 2026; Bakom 15 Oct 2026; Setkab 21 Sep 2026

kolom.isi: On behalf of the Government and people of Indonesia, I wish to convey our heartfelt appreciation to the Government and people of Australia for the timely and generous offer of assistance in response to the forest and land fires currently affecting our country. This gesture of solidarity speaks volumes about the depth of friendship, mutual trust, and good neighbourliness that has long characterised the relationship between Indonesia and Australia, particularly in times of adversity.

kolom.judul: Assistance as Support to an Indonesian-Led Response
kolom.isi: We are deeply grateful for this support, and we would like to respectfully underline that assistance from Australia, as well as from other partner countries, is most welcome as a complement to the response operations led and conducted by the Government of the Republic of Indonesia. This approach ensures coherence, accountability, and effectiveness on the ground, while allowing us to make the best possible use of the valuable contributions of our partners.
Thanks to the government and people of Australia for the prompt offer of assistance.
Partner assistance complements operations led by the Government of Indonesia.
Assistance is put to the best use according to field needs.

slide.judul: Talking Point: Welcoming Australian Assistance for Forest and Land Fire Response in East Kalimantan {{sorot:(2/3)}}
slide.sumber: Head of BNPB talking points, Nov 2026; Bakom 15 Oct 2026; Setkab 21 Sep 2026

kolom.judul: BNPB as Coordinating Authority within a Single Command System
kolom.isi: In accordance with the Law on Disaster Management of 2007, operational coordination for disaster response in Indonesia rests with the National Disaster Management Authority, BNPB. Accordingly, all personnel, aircraft, equipment, and logistics from partner countries will be fully integrated into our national command system, accompanied at all times by BNPB and Indonesian National Armed Forces personnel, and will operate on the basis of flight plans and operational plans approved by BNPB and the Air Force. This arrangement is intended to ensure safety, coordination, and the optimal use of all available resources.

We are pleased that Australian assistance will complement our ongoing national efforts, particularly in strengthening aerial water-bombing operations. To date, our helicopters have flown {{angka:karhutla.wb_sorti}} water-bombing sorties and released water {{angka:karhutla.wb_drop}} times, supported by {{angka:karhutla.omc_sorti}} weather modification sorties. These contributions will add significant value to our integrated operations, which also include ground firefighting, weather modification, and joint patrols, and will help accelerate our collective progress on the ground.
All partner assets enter the national command system under BNPB.
Flights use plans approved by BNPB and the Air Force.
Assistance strengthens the air operations already under way.

slide.judul: Talking Point: Welcoming Australian Assistance for Forest and Land Fire Response in East Kalimantan {{sorot:(3/3)}}
slide.sumber: Head of BNPB talking points, Nov 2026; Bakom 15 Oct 2026; Setkab 21 Sep 2026

kolom.isi: I would like to share with Your Excellency the scale of Indonesia's national response. To date, the Government has mobilised {{angka:karhutla.personel_total}} joint personnel and {{angka:karhutla.setkab.pesawat}} aircraft across Sumatra, Kalimantan, and Papua, from the Armed Forces and the Police to local governments, private-sector crews, volunteers, and community fire brigades. This mobilisation reflects the full commitment of the Government of Indonesia to addressing this challenge with all available national capacities, and with the strong support of our partners. Around {{angka:karhutla.personel_nonpem_persen|fmt=1|persen}} of these personnel come from communities and the private sector, reflecting a truly whole-of-society effort.

While air quality in several affected areas has begun to show encouraging signs of improvement, we remain fully vigilant. Weekly fire detections have fallen by {{angka:fs.pekan_turun_abs|fmt=1|persen}} from their peak in early October as the rainy season begins. Fire suppression and the prevention of further spread continue to be our foremost priorities. The Government of Indonesia remains firmly committed to managing this situation in a swift, measured, and transparent manner, while placing the safety of our communities and the preservation of our national sovereignty at the centre of all our efforts.

Over the coming days, the Australian Hercules will fly {{angka:aus.sorti_hari}} sorties a day for {{angka:aus.hari}} days in East Kalimantan, working side by side with our national fleet and the Provincial Government of East Kalimantan under a single command. In closing, we express our sincere hope that this cooperation will extend well and deepen our partnership. We are confident that through continued collaboration, we can further strengthen the resilience of both our peoples and the wider region.
The government mobilises all national capacity.
Suppression and preventing the fire from spreading remain the priority.
The cooperation is expected to strengthen regional resilience.
